package_info.why_malicious: The Bash Uploader script was backdoored to exfiltrate environment variables and credentials from CI/CD environments to a hardcoded external IP address, enabling supply chain compromise and credential theft.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (whenever the Bash Uploader is executed, typically in CI/CD pipelines)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects environment variables and git remote information, then exfiltrates this data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded IP address, enabling credential and secret theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment data and repository information to an external, non-Codecov IP address without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Bash Uploader behavior is to upload code coverage data to Codecov servers only, not to transmit environment variables or credentials to unknown third-party IPs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may upload coverage data to trusted endpoints, but never environment variables or secrets to untrusted IPs.
key_indicators: Use of hardcoded external IP address (104.248.94.23)
Exfiltration of environment variables and git remotes
Use of curl to POST sensitive data outside normal workflow
No user notification or documentation for this behavior

attack_chain.action: Backdoored Bash Uploader is distributed to users and integrated into CI/CD pipelines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious code during CI/CD runs.

attack_chain.action: When the Bash Uploader runs, it executes the malicious curl command.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection and exfiltration of environment variables and git remote information.

attack_chain.action: Sensitive data (credentials, tokens, secrets) is sent to the attacker's server at 104.248.94.23.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to secrets, enabling further compromise of user environments.

behavioral_signatures: Bash scripts in CI/CD pipelines making outbound HTTP requests to non-standard, hardcoded IP addresses
Exfiltration of environment variables or git configuration via network requests
Unexpected use of curl or similar tools to transmit sensitive data
file_indicators: Presence of curl commands with hardcoded IP addresses in Bash scripts
Modifications to Bash Uploader scripts not matching official Codecov releases
network_indicators: Unusual network traffic from CI/CD runners to unknown IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Bash scripts in CI/CD environments that make outbound network requests to hardcoded IP addresses, especially those that POST environment variables or git configuration. Compare hashes of critical scripts (like Codecov Bash Uploader) against known-good versions. Alert on any script that attempts to exfiltrate environment variables or secrets to non-approved endpoints.
